boards.title: PIXEL ART
boards.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a professional game art-direction comparison storyboard, ONE finished image. Create a large landscape art board titled exactly "01 / PIXEL ART". Arrange FIVE equally important wide gameplay scene panels in a clean layout: two columns in the first two rows, and one wide fifth panel across the bottom. Label each panel with its code and short title. This is a stylistic comparison board, not a UI dashboard. Artwork fills at least 90% of the page, very narrow dark gutters, no prose or stats tables.
The original game is turn-based scrap-magnet combat. In EVERY panel depict the SAME functional scene from an easily readable fixed SIDE VIEW: a squat operator's forge-cannon platform on the left, a recognisable heavy horseshoe industrial magnet hanging by a chain above a heap of stacked steel nuts, toothed gears and bolts; a few metal pieces being drawn visibly up toward its poles; an upright three-part physical ammunition assembly (steel body, small bright payload capsule, pointed cap) being loaded into the cannon; a mounted protective metal plate; two distinct hostile scrap robots on the right. Keep all subjects big enough to read, open separation between rig and enemies, depth only in backgrounds, no top-down or isometric board. Subtle compact health bars and a few energy pips are allowed, no card deck or card UI.
All five panels must be genuinely PIXEL ART with deliberately placed hard square pixels, no blurred pixels, not a 3D render with a pixel filter. Vary structure, resolution, texture, shape language and lighting, not just hue:
01A / 8-BIT: severe chunky low-resolution sprites, 4-colour-per-object look, black contours, simple bold scenery.
01B / 16-BIT: richly authored 1990s arcade pixel sprites, detailed industrial forms, stepped highlights, readable parallax layers.
01C / NEON PIXELS: limited deep navy backdrop, vivid emissive pixel bands and sparks, futuristic silhouettes, sharp pixels preserved.
01D / MINIATURE: tiny diorama-like pixel machinery with careful clustered detail, warm daylight, intimate handcrafted miniature scale, still side view.
01E / NANO PIXELS: ultra-coarse micro-sprites and extremely economical large pixel clusters, dramatic negative space, only a handful of pixels describe each bolt or enemy. Intentionally more abstract than 01A but still recognisable.
Each scene should feel like a polished original indie game worth buying, with a satisfying magnetic pull and clear potential for weapon impact. No franchise characters, logos, watermarks, realistic humans, dense text or beige PowerPoint layout. This board explores one family; do not introduce watercolour, clay, vector or photographic styles.
boards.review: static visual inspection in generated tool output
boards.observation: All five coded variants present. The very coarse treatment loses individual part identity; 16-bit/miniature variants preserve more detail. Pixel labels describe an aesthetic, not hardware-accurate sprites.

boards.prompt:

The comparison is only the rendering depth and camera, so use the SAME original forge-cannon, operator, horseshoe magnet hanging on a chain, upright component-loaded ammunition assembly, protective plate, pile of loose gears and bolts, two enemy scrap robots, same warm/cool palette and same understated environment in all three. Restrained health bars and energy pips, no card interface. The player must instantly understand what each object is. A clear close view, art fills the page with very narrow gutters, not a PowerPoint slide.
Frame 16A label "16A / 2D SPRITES": completely flat illustrated side-view sprites with confident simple contours, lateral silhouettes, flat colour shading, all action in a single readable plane, illustrated background layers.
Frame 16B label "16B / 2.5D SIDE VIEW": the same scene and layout seen side-on, with appealing sculpted 3D models, visible thickness and bevels, real contact shadows, foreground and background parallax. Gameplay is visibly on one lateral plane but objects have volume, suspended chain curves and swinging parts show weight. No overhead view.
Frame 16C label "16C / 3D PERSPECTIVE": same models as B but a clearly different three-quarter perspective camera looking across the rig toward the scrap pile and enemies; visible depth and foreshortening, some natural occlusion demonstrates the depth tradeoff. Not first person and not top-down.
No additional visual styles, no franchise references, no slogans, no explanatory paragraphs, no charts. The presentation should make flat artwork, layered side-view depth and free spatial perspective visibly different without making A look deliberately worse. All are polished legitimate game options.
